correctness.rationale: Quotient differentiation gives w_iw_j(s_j−s_i)(λ_i−λ_j) at exponent λ_i+λ_j in the positive-denominator derivative. Merge equal rates by their weighted mean scores; if the resulting mean is constant it has no strict reversal (the derivative-zero bound is for a nonzero numerator). For three distinct rates the three ordered coefficients cannot alternate twice, by transitivity of the effective scores. In the four-class rate cone, the ordered pair signs are −−−++−; at a tied middle pair, collecting coefficients cannot add a sign change. The generalized Descartes bound follows by dividing by the lowest power and differentiating: Rolle counts multiplicity, and with equal first two coefficient signs the normalized function initially moves away from zero, so an additional derivative zero is needed before the first root. For the witness, after division by 50y⁴ with y=e^(−t), the exact coefficients are (−3,−6,−16,100,100,−200); evaluations at y=1,1/2,1/4 give −25, 5/2, −479/128. The two disjoint sign brackets saturate the multiplicity bound, giving two simple roots and a minimum followed by a maximum. The finite-depth brackets and strict hypotheses persist under small simultaneous perturbations. Monotone rate-vs-score order precludes reversals by the pair formula. The attached checker was inspected, not executed. The rate-sum condition is sufficient but not necessary for the upper bound; the original does not assert necessity.

evidence: Lemma 2.3(b) characterizes an extended complete Chebyshev system by nonvanishing initial Wronskians, implying at most dimension minus one zeros counting multiplicity for a nonzero linear combination.

The ratio paper's order-three sign-regular theorem explicitly addresses unimodal coefficient ratios and exponential kernels; the four-score ranks here are not unimodal, so that theorem alone is not used to cover four rates.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Sort rates increasingly, set e_i=exp(−λ_it), and B=Σ w_ie_i. For k=1,…,m−1, the prefix Wronskian of ((e_1/B)′,…,(e_k/B)′) equals W(1,e_1/B,…,e_k/B)=B^(−k−1)W(B,e_1,…,e_k). Expanding in B leaves only j>k terms w_j W(e_j,e_1,…,e_k). They all have the same nonzero sign: each is a positive exponential times a Vandermonde on the ordered distinct exponents, with the same permutation of columns. Thus apply the known criterion to the entire derivative basis. Since e_m/B is affine in the first m−1 ratios, M′ is in the span. This yields m−2 zeros for nonconstant M, without the extra four-rate hypothesis.

originality.rationale: The main upper bound is a routine specialization of a verified classical extended Chebyshev-system criterion to the normalized exponential basis: in fact any nonconstant mean with m positive rate groups has at most m−2 stationary zeros, independently of rate gaps and score order. The earlier shared-rate mortality result is mathematically equivalent to the three-rate obstruction and supplies a four-rate attaining witness in the present ordering after a reciprocal/time-reversal reduction and a small rate perturbation. The reported numerical filtration example can differ without supplying a distinct sharp theorem.
residual_risks: Exact historical priority for the derivative-basis specialization is not claimed. The verdict rests on demonstrated implication and overlap rather than matching titles.
The Pinelis oscillation paper and Boos et al. full text were unavailable; neither is needed to infer the coverage established here.

value.rationale: The diagnostic is intelligible as a model illustration, but the main mathematical conclusion is a routine specialization of the general Chebyshev zero count, with a superfluous gap restriction; the constrained two-turn existence is also accessible by direct reparametrization of an earlier exact witness. The arbitrary hypothetical weights and depth numerics add no established empirical or independently useful exact invariant. There is no validation of the one-peaked condition in filtration data.
